articles.title: Saved for Sunday: Robert Pattinson and James Bond’s baggage problem
articles.summary: After years of speculation, there’s a new 007 in town. Today Sian Cain explains why Bond has so much ‘baggage’ and what we might expect from Robert Pattinson in the role. Want Saved For Sunday in your inbox every weekend? Sign up here, and why not share it with a friend.
body: Leading questions: I’m engaged, but I can’t stop thinking about an old friend. Should I tell him how I feel?

What to watch | Catholic schoolgirls rule in “gleefully camp” coming of age horror The Body, new to Netflix. Set in 2004, it’ll give millennial viewers flashbacks, but adds a dash of satanic ritual to the trope-y teen dramas of the era.

What to play | Possibly the most anticipated video game of all time, 13 years in the making, Grand Theft Auto VI dropped this week. It earned five stars from our games editor. She spent more than 70 hours playing it through, and says it could have taken longer, so while claims of the GTA Flu may be greatly exaggerated, you might need to take close to two weeks off to finish it.

What to read | In Gary Shteyngart’s first book of nonfiction essays, The Sensualist, the comic novelist wants to make you feel good. Devoted to the pursuit of pleasure, from icy martinis with Gerri from Succession, to a trip to South America to meet capybaras, his adventures and style may be silly, but they’re often sharp too.

articles.title: The Australian fashion artisans who still make clothes by hand
articles.summary: The meticulous process of hand-stitching clothing and footwear is rare in Australia, but the ateliers who do so are attracting a new generation of clients and colleagues. Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email.
body: In a world where garment makers are forced to wear AI-training headgear and T-shirts can be ordered from Kmart on Uber Eats, it may seem as if the days of procuring something made by hand from an artisan are numbered.

While jobs in Australian textile, clothing and footwear manufacturing have been in freefall since their 1989 peak – from 115,000 to approximately 30,000 in 2026 – the work of a dressmaker or shoemaker who stitches every piece by hand is even harder to find.
But in certain studios and fitting rooms around the country, tape measures are wielded, fabric is pinched and pinned and the warmth of service extends well beyond holding out an Eftpos machine.

For hand-makers, the work is about more than just another product or a paycheck. The beauty of their vocation is in many small acts: mastering technique, appreciating texture, building a community of clients, and drawing on the mysterious well of creative intuition that allows humans to make wonderful things.

articles.title: The moment I knew: She flew me to the scene of my favourite romantic movie
articles.summary: Kaz Therese had always loved An Affair to Remember. A few months into their relationship, Brianna surprised her with a magical gift. Find more stories from the moment I knew series.
body: Brianna and I met in 2013 on an arts project I was developing in Mount Druitt, the region I grew up in, in western Sydney.
It was a site-specific work for young people, and Brianna became part of the strategic leadership team, which ultimately meant she was painting gutters pink with the local kids until 9pm each night.

Our first meeting was electric – we had so much in common, I felt as if I’d been donged on the head. Through the work, I was trying to push back against the stigma of Mount Druitt and create something fun and magical, and she understood the importance of what I was trying to do. After the project, I got a position running a theatre company nearby, and I invited her on to the board.

We were both in relationships at the time and I was coming out of a deeply unhappy one. For those first two years working together, I had a secret crush on her. A few months later we were both single and I invited her over to help write a grant together for a project I hoped to do in Berlin. That week happened to be my birthday, and a friend had given me a bottle of Moët, which I planned to save for a special occasion.

articles.title: Too lazy for lawns? Try a native meadow
articles.summary: Exotic lawns require a tradeoff between ease and beauty. While Australian native grasses take longer to establish, they can be worth the wait. Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email. Do you yearn for that suburban dream, the perfect lawn?
body: Do you yearn to join one of those neighbourhood groups whose members compete to show off the result – the kind of people who use laser levels and precision bombing with biological weapons to achieve grassy perfection?
“There’s no grass that ticks all the boxes,” says Melbourne landscaper Simon McCurdy. “Each has its positive attributes and drawbacks.”

In his 38 years of experience, McCurdy has seen roll-out turf largely displace seed-sowing for lawn establishment. “Virtually all our clients want instant results,” he says. “And when you factor in the time involved in sowing from seed it’s certainly cheaper for most people to install turf.”

For larger areas McCurdy says many people choose hydroseeding, an intermediate method between seeding and turf, in which emulsions of seed, water, mulch and fertiliser are sprayed on to prepared soil. But which grass variety to choose?

articles.title: The 8 Best James Bond Films
articles.summary: As we await Robert Pattinson’s first outing as 007, these are the classics worth revisiting now.
body: Terrible puns. Rampant misogyny. Disposable female characters. A frequently stale rotation of vodka martinis, gun fights, and stiff-upper-lip bureaucracy. Bond movies are very easy to make fun of—and, let’s face it, of the 25 that have so far been released over the past six decades, a majority are pretty forgettable. But there are a handful that are worth watching, even if you actively abhor the subgenre.
Following Robert Pattinson’s appointment as the new 007, we present eight Bond films that are actually decent. May more follow!

Where it all began. A suave Sean Connery, Ursula Andress as the bikini-clad Honey Ryder, the pristine white beaches of Jamaica… this Terence Young-helmed first installment of the franchise laid the blueprint for everything that followed, but is also a thoroughly entertaining romp in its own right. It’s easy to see why it became a box-office bonanza and birthed a cultural phenomenon that endures to this day.

articles.title: ‘Cancer Does Change You’: Kate Middleton Shares Her Healing Journey in ‘Deeply Personal’ Documentary
articles.summary: Kate Middleton, the Princess of Wales, has shared the trailer for an emotional new documentary, ‘Heal,’ in which she charts her cancer journey.
body: “Cancer does change you,” Kate Middleton says in the emotional trailer for the film, Heal. The Princess of Wales is to release a “deeply personal” documentary, in which she will discuss her cancer diagnosis, her journey towards healing, and navigating life after experiencing serious illness.

In the clip, we see cameras trailing the Princess as she completes the Three Peaks —one of the UK’s toughest hiking challenges—which happened earlier this year. “It changes your body, it changes you physically,” she continues. “But there’s a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you.” In June, the mum-of-three scaled the highest mountains in Scotland (Ben Nevis), England (Scafell Pike), and Wales (Snowdon) within 24 hours. Kate, who just completed a visit to Mumbai, India, with the Prince of Wales for the 2026 Earthshot Prize ceremony, had announced that her cancer was in remission in January 2025.

Footage in the trailer shows the Princess approaching a summit in foggy conditions, and tearfully hugging her children, George, Charlotte, and Louis, and her husband, Prince William, after completing her challenge.

articles.title: Can a Pre-Nup Be Romantic?
articles.summary: Prenups can help ease wedding-planning tension and build long-term trust—here, relationship experts break down how to navigate the money talk with transparency and care.
body: Budgeting, filling out tax forms together, managing family dynamics, and standing in line at city hall: not sexy. Not romantic. Alas, they are the mundane mechanics of even the most thrilling of married lives. Soon after a ring is on the finger, many couples are now discussing prenups—and it’s a topic that brings up unglamorous realities.

No, the administrative process of a prenup isn’t inherently romantic, and let’s not pretend it is. But what it does for the relationship—laying everything bare with radical honesty—is deeply romantic.

“I think navigating something that’s challenging in a relationship and coming out of it aligned is romantic, sexy, and empowering,” says Ashley Hesseltine. The co-host of Girls Gotta Eat spoke openly about choosing to have a prenuptial agreement with her now husband. “But I will not lie. The process of a prenup is inherently annoying, unsexy, and invasive. And it’s admin.”

Wedding planning has a way of sweeping us up into a whirlwind of floral arrangements, seating charts, and linen swatches. Conversations about money, family expectations, and core values naturally come to the forefront next to celebrations.
points: Prenups can help ease wedding-planning tension and build long-term trust—here, relationship experts break down how to navigate the money talk with transparency and care.

articles.title: Sienna Spiro Had Herself a Merry Little Christmas at the Bloomingdale’s x Ralph Lauren Window Unveiling
articles.summary: On Friday evening, as crowds swarmed Lexington Avenue and 59th Street to catch a glimpse of the breakthrough singer, Spiro was on hand to unveil the Bloomingdale’s holiday windows, created this season in collaboration with Ralph Lauren.
body: “It’s my first time seeing New York at Christmas. I didn’t even know this [opportunity] was an option. I’m so happy about it,” Spiro told Vogue in the greenroom ahead of the public performance. Even in the context of her “whirlwind” year, it had been quite the week: On Monday, she was announced as a contender for Best New Artist at the 2027 Grammys, and on Wednesday, her name appeared on the lineup for next summer’s Glastonbury festival. “This year has been just insane,” she said. “There’s no fancy word for it. Something new has happened every single day. I can’t really keep up with it to be honest.”

For her latest surreal career moment, the rising star donned a glossy red mackintosh coat from the Ralph Lauren archives, which she paired with black leather driving gloves and sky-high Louboutins—very in keeping with her youthful spin on a vintage-esque look that has been keeping her fans enthralled.
